messages:
emily: Quick note from support: customers copying the Go quickstart into HTTP handlers are hitting generator hangups because the example constructs client with context.Background().

rafa: We should clarify in our quickstart that the client may be long-lived, but individual streaming calls must use the request context. Example: `gen := client.Generator(r.Context(), req)` and `defer gen.Close()` immediately.

noah: Found a secondary issue: our retry/backoff helper uses time.Sleep(jitter) which doesn't observe ctx.Done(), so canceled requests still block during retries. I changed that to `t := time.NewTimer(j); select { case <-t.C: ; case <-ctx.Done(): t.Stop(); return ctx.Err() }`.

emily: Filed issue #3490 with a tiny repro and heap goroutine stack. I'll link to sample-app that reproduces the leak.

build-bot: build #7210 for branch fix/go-gen-ctx landed: all tests passed :white_check_mark:

rafa: We should add a small integration test that starts a generator, cancels ctx, and asserts goroutine count returns to baseline within 100ms to catch regressions.

noah: Also thinking about API ergonomics: `Generator` returns a stream that has Close(). Some streams are inconsistent in naming (CloseStream/Shutdown). Propose standardizing to Close() across the SDK. Opened RFC issue for API parity.

emily: For docs change, add a brief sidebar: "Avoid context.Background() for request-scoped streams. Use request context or context.WithTimeout." and update quickstart snippet.

rafa: I'll submit the docs PR and link the retry patch and test. cc @noah.

emily: Thanks — good catch.
